figures.caption: Figure 3.2: MS-RCGR trajectories for the example sequence ATCGATCGTAGC across scales k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}. Each trajectory is initiated at the origin × and progresses through nk = n−k+1 points (indicated in each panel), with edge opacity encoding temporal order. The star marker (⋆) denotes the final position p (k) nk , which forms the first component of the per-scale descriptor φ(k)(s) (Eq. 3.4). As k increases, k-mer tokenisation reduces the effective sequence length and maps overlapping windows onto a coarser alphabet, producing trajectories with fewer but geometrically distinct points that capture progressively longer-range compositional patterns.

Figure 3.1: MS-RCGR-based Representation of the example DNA sequence ATCGATCGTAGC at scale k = 1. Corner points for nucleotides A, T, G, and C are placed on the unit circle via rational-arithmetic trigonometric assignment (Eq. 3.1). The trajectory is initiated at the origin p0 = (0, 0) and each successive point pt is computed as the midpoint between pt−1 and the corner of the current nucleotide (Eq. 3.2). Points are coloured by their corresponding nucleotide, and progressive darkening of trajectory edges reflects sequence order.
